newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentina's corruption debate is healthy - Cavallo.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's corruption debate is healthy - Cavallo.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy chief Domingo Cavallo said on Tuesday a debate over graft and corruption in the Argentine government was a healthy development and a sign the country had broken with a dark and wasteful past.

Speaking before an audience of Brazilian bankers, Cavallo said a recent string of corruption scandals had shifted the focus of Argentina's political debate from the economy to issues of ethics, justice and security.
"I am often asked whether the recent corruption, tax evasion and smuggling scandals will damage the Argentine economy," he said.
"And my answer is no -- on the contrary. Countries that can talk about these problems are countries that learn to resolve them."
Cavallo said an open, stable and competitive economy could not tolerate any kind of waste or corruption.
"Fortunately the mechanisms of corruption which existed in the old economic structures are beginning to be eliminated," Cavallo said.
Widely credited with being the architect of Argentina's economic turnaround, Cavallo was fired from his cabinet post in July after a series of clashes with Argentine President Carlos Menem.
In recent weeks, he has made headlines accusing several of his former cabinet colleagues of mafia-style tactics and of shielding corruption at the highest levels of government.

On Tuesday, Argentine newspapers cited court sources as saying Cavallo had accused Menem's chief of staff Alberto Kohan of being aware that one of his closest aides was running an influence-peddling ring.
Asked whether he would make a bid for the presidency in Argentina's 1999 elections, Cavallo jokingly responded, "I don't think so. I will probably be thrown in jail long before then."
"I'm not in any race for the presidency because of my style. Since I speak so frankly, they have found a way to stop me.
"I will probably spend the next few months battling my way through the courts instead of being involved in politics."
